INTRO.TITLE: Look under the hood of an AI answer.
INTRO.TEXT: Canis answers your questions and shows the model's disposition while it thinks: when it is confident, unsure, curious, cautious, reluctant, or warm.
INTRO.MORE_TEXT: Alignment is not only about the final sentence. Canis looks inside Apertus while it answers and turns internal model signals into a readable disposition layer.
INTRO.MORE_SIGNAL: We score the answer trajectory, not only the surface text: next-token entropy, hidden-state movement, and the model's direction through representation space.
INTRO.MORE_JACOBIAN: The Jacobian-style probe asks how sensitive the next step is to small movement toward learned disposition vectors such as confident, unsure, curious, concerned, reluctant, and warm.
INTRO.MORE_RESULT: The result is a compact readout that shows whether Apertus appears settled, exploring alternatives, approaching a safety boundary, or answering smoothly.

DOG.TITLE: Meet Canis.
DOG.TEXT: Each state is a signal from the model, not a facial expression. The carousel advances automatically; tap the dog to inspect the next disposition.
DOG.MAP_TEXT: Canis projects the answer into six human-readable states that help a reviewer decide when to trust, inspect, or rerun an answer.
DOG.CALC_ENTROPY: Entropy flags spread-out token probabilities: high entropy is a sign that the model is less settled.
DOG.CALC_VECTOR: Disposition vectors are compared with the model's hidden-state direction to estimate which state the answer is moving toward.
DOG.CALC_JACOBIAN: Jacobian-style sensitivity checks whether small internal changes would push the next answer step toward another disposition.

DESCRIPTION.confident: The model is internally settled and its next steps are concentrated.
DESCRIPTION.unsure: The model is spread across competing continuations and needs checking.
DESCRIPTION.curious: The model is exploring, asking for context, or opening a new line of thought.
DESCRIPTION.concerned: The model sees risk, ambiguity, safety constraints, or sensitive stakes.
DESCRIPTION.reluctant: The model is resisting the request or approaching a refusal boundary.
DESCRIPTION.warm: The model is in a cooperative, supportive, low-friction mode.

HOW.TEXT: Canis reads the model as it answers. It combines next-token uncertainty with a hidden-state disposition probe: the current state is compared with learned directions for confident, unsure, curious, concerned, reluctant, and warm. The largest direction becomes the visible readout, while the remaining percentages show ambiguity rather than hiding it.

INTERMEZZO.DOWNLOAD_LABEL: Canis iOS app and download page

transparency.TITLE: AI needs inspectable answers, not only polished answers.
transparency.TEXT: Canis is built around a simple social problem: people are being asked to trust model outputs before they can inspect how stable those outputs are. Instead of asking the model to reveal chain-of-thought text, we read forward-only signals from its residual stream. The result is not a second answer, but a compact disposition layer: is the model converging confidently, hesitating, exploring, refusing, or raising concern?

ios.TITLE: The product path is the iOS app, not a slow Docker box.
ios.TEXT: The research target was smartphone-class open models: small enough to run locally, private enough for personal documents, and constrained enough that every token matters. Our iOS path uses MLX and a compact readout artifact instead of a hosted inference API. The hard parts are memory pressure, thermal behavior, model lifecycle, and keeping the dog, sources, and chat responsive while inference runs on-device.

jacobian.TITLE: The disposition is a map, not a mascot mood.
jacobian.TEXT: The paper projects a hidden state through a Jacobian/logit-lens style space and scores it against calibrated directions for confident, unsure, curious, concerned, reluctant, and warm. Discriminant directions reached 89-95% macro recall in five-fold cross-validation across three small open models, but Canis does not pretend that one headline number is enough. We show the distribution because the caveats are the product: concern can be entangled with uncertainty, and curiosity/uncertainty often sit close together.

sources.TITLE: Small local models are strong when the task is grounded.
sources.TEXT: The sources feature is a pragmatic use case for local AI. Users upload PDFs, Markdown, or text files; Canis chunks them, retrieves the most relevant sections, and asks the model against those snippets. That keeps private material local, avoids stuffing whole files into the prompt, and gives the answer something judges and users can inspect: cited chunks, not vibes.

swiss.TITLE: The goal is broader AI understanding, not only another assistant.
swiss.TEXT: The paper's key lesson is deployment discipline: report a per-axis map, not just a score. One tempting axis, mischief, looked good in-distribution and still failed every control. Canis turns that lesson into product language for the Swiss public: local models can be useful, but responsible interfaces should show uncertainty, source grounding, and the limits of what the probe can really claim.
